title: From Consent to Rehab: Orthopedic Language Access
summary: Build an orthopedic language access pathway for consent, surgery, discharge, weight-bearing instructions, rehabilitation, and follow-up.
body_markdown:
###


Use return demonstration for crutches, walkers, transfers, stairs, braces, equipment, and home exercises. Pair it with teach-back for medications, warning signs, and follow-up.


###


Name the limb, permitted load, duration, device, prohibited actions, and contact for conflicting instructions. Ask the patient to explain and show the plan.


###


Family members may support the patient, but they should not be the default clinical interpreters. Use approved language support and define the family member’s role.


###


Transfer the procedure, current restrictions, equipment, medication changes, warning signs, follow-up, language needs, and any unresolved communication issue.


###


Track language-data accuracy, failed sessions, teach-back, return demonstrations, conflicting instructions, medication discrepancies, missed therapy, callbacks, complaints, and corrective actions.
